main_text.p: noftri corporis nutritione ullam attra- ctionem admitto, nisi quòd cordis dilatatione per internam quandam fermentationem adaucta, Cor ipsum flatuam vitalis anthię inflatque succum quemcunque in suas cavitates allicere, (de qua re egi Exercit. de Chylif. & Chyli motu f. 53. 54. & 67. itemque Differt. de Motu Cord. & Sang. §. 8 & 11. nec non Comm. ibid.) flatuamque per at- tractionem Aërem infpirando in Pulmo-nes adduci, quod itidem oftendi Exer-cit. de Respir. §. 48. &seqq. ita nec Plan- tas exiftimo allicere alimentum; sed succum quemcunque vi radiorum folarium agitatum ac refolutum in tenuem vaporem, excipere in radices, atque ex tali lucco non nisi eas atomos admittere, quæ poris cujusque plantæ sunt congruæ ac proportionatæ.
Sed Illuftriffimi Viri veftigia porro sequamur; ipsamque luftremus Filtra-tionem, ubi corpus humidum per aliud ficcum adscendit. Rectè inquit Vir Il-luftr.

page.notes: Lower part of the page is faint; the final words are at the page edge. Some words in the first paragraph (e.g. "inflatque", "succum") are uncertain and may be misread; the transcription reflects the scan as best read. Some letters are blurred around "Plantas"; marked as read.
